name: Application and Product Security
guide:
Application and Product Security work centers on building security into products before they ship rather than attacking them after the fact. Day to day, that means secure code review, threat modeling design documents before features are built, and working directly with engineering teams to fix vulnerabilities inside the software development lifecycle. Reviewers here look at pull requests, CI/CD pipelines, and API designs rather than running red team engagements against a live network. This is different from Offensive Security, which focuses on penetration testing and simulated attacks against systems that already exist, and it differs from general Security Engineering, which more often covers cloud infrastructure, identity, and network defense rather than the product's own codebase. In our data, postings labeled Application Security or Product Security consistently pair those words with threat modeling, secure SDLC, and vulnerability management rather than exploit development.

On credentials, our sample of 130 tracked postings does not name a single specific certification like OSCP or CSSLP in the structured skill data employers listed. That is worth saying plainly rather than filling in a certification employers didn't actually ask for. What does appear repeatedly are compliance and framework references such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, FedRAMP, NIST, and GDPR, which point to employers wanting familiarity with security standards and audits more than a personal exam badge. A computer science or related technical degree shows up as an expectation at large or regulated employers like Kaiser Permanente and Booz Allen Hamilton, though many startup and AI company listings in our data emphasize hands-on experience over a degree requirement. Treat a named certification as a plus rather than a gate, based on what we are actually seeing posted.

Experience requirements in our tracked postings skew toward the middle of the career ladder. Of 130 postings, 67 are labeled mid-level, 30 senior, 19 staff, 9 manager, and the rest split between lead, principal, and one executive role. That means the bulk of hiring right now is for engineers with a few years of hands-on application security or software engineering experience, not entry-level roles and not exclusively senior architects. What tends to get someone hired at the mid-level is direct experience fixing vulnerabilities inside a real codebase and working closely with developers, while staff and senior roles in our data lean on distributed systems, cryptography, and the ability to set security standards across multiple teams.

The technical skill list drawn from our postings is dominated by Application Security itself, appearing in 73 of 130 rows, followed closely by Threat Modeling at 60 and Rust at 58. AWS, CI/CD, and Python also appear over 40 times each, and Vulnerability Management, Penetration Testing, and Large Language Models each show up around 30 times, reflecting how many of these roles now sit inside AI companies. Java, Kubernetes, GCP, TypeScript, and Azure round out the next tier, and the named tools skew toward cloud platforms and languages rather than specific SAST or DAST product names, which our current data does not capture in detail. Companies posting in this category are clearly building security into modern cloud native and AI product stacks rather than legacy on-premise software.

Right now we currently track approximately 54 open postings in Application and Product Security, out of 130 total postings we have seen in this category. Of those 130, 51 postings included both a minimum and maximum salary figure, and among that group pay ranged from $86,775 to $288,991 a year, with average figures landing near $159,000 to $163,000. Anthropic and Kaiser Permanente each appear 6 times in our tracked postings, followed by Writer and ServiceNow at 5 each, and Harvey, Okta, OpenAI, and Booz Allen Hamilton at 4 each. That mix of frontier AI labs, established tech platforms, and large regulated employers shows this discipline is in demand across very different kinds of companies right now.
